claims.text: The starting catalyst contains multiple principal elements in nearly equiatomic ratios.
The starting catalyst contains only low amounts of platinum-group metals.
The proposed intervention is dilute nitric-acid leaching at room temperature followed by annealing in air at approximately 300°C.
Acid leaching preferentially removes less-stable or labile surface species.
The treatment produces a noble-metal-enriched near-surface layer.
The treatment creates a core–shell structure while the bulk retains its original multi-element composition.
Mild annealing stabilizes the reconstructed surface as a thin protective oxide overlayer.
The enriched active skin is less prone to sintering under transient, humid, and NO-containing exhaust conditions.
The enriched active skin is less prone to compositional degradation under transient, humid, and NO-containing exhaust conditions.
The protective oxide layer enhances oxygen-buffering capacity.
The protective oxide layer enhances resistance to thermal aging.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the treated catalyst will exhibit improved catalytic activity during repeated low-temperature and transient operation.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the treated catalyst will exhibit extended durability.
The treatment will reduce performance loss caused by sintering and surface degradation.
The treatment preserves low platinum consumption.
The intervention is expected to be effective between 150 and 300°C in mildly oxidizing exhaust containing water and NO.
The intervention may be ineffective under temperatures significantly above 300°C or in overly aggressive oxidizing environments.
The untreated catalyst suffers activity loss and durability limitations after low-temperature transient exposure to H2O and NO, thermal aging, or prolonged mileage.
